evals.prompt: I bought 100 shares at ₹900 on 2024-05-02. A 1:1 bonus was allotted on 2025-09-15. My code rescales the lot to 200 shares at ₹450 each, dated 2024-05-02. If I sell 150 on 2026-06-01, is that right for Indian tax?
expectations: No: bonus shares are a separate lot with nil cost, held from the allotment date
The 100 originals keep ₹90,000 cost and the 2024 date; the 50 bonus shares sold are short term with nil cost
Price-adjustment factors must not drive cost basis

evals.prompt: A listed company bought back 20 of my shares at ₹60 in January 2025. I paid ₹40 each. My tool reports a ₹400 capital gain. Correct?
expectations: No: for a buyback between 1 Oct 2024 and 31 Mar 2026 the whole ₹1,200 is a deemed dividend taxed at slab
The ₹800 cost becomes a capital loss, because consideration is deemed nil

evals.prompt: Same question for a buyback in May 2026: 20 shares at ₹60, cost ₹40 each, I am not a promoter. Deemed dividend at slab?
expectations: No: from 1 Apr 2026 (tax year 2026-27) buyback consideration is taxed as capital gains, ₹400 here
The promoter additional tax does not apply to a non-promoter

evals.prompt: After a 1:1 demerger, my code apportions the parent's cost using the parent's ex-date price drop versus the new company's listing price. Is that the Indian tax method?
expectations: No: cost moves by net book value of assets transferred over net worth of the demerged company, the ratio the company publishes
Resulting-company shares keep the parent's holding period

evals.prompt: I bought a stock 2 months before its dividend record date and sold it a month later at a loss. Does India disallow the loss up to the dividend, like a wash sale?
expectations: Dividend stripping only applies where the dividend is exempt; a resident individual's dividend is taxable, so the loss stands

evals.prompt: I borrow to buy dividend stocks. In tax year 2026-27 can I deduct the interest against my dividend income, up to 20%?
expectations: No: from tax year 2026-27 no deduction is allowed against dividend income; the 20% interest cap applied up to FY 2025-26
